samples.summary: Table-cell "No fill" reset still cannot clear the stored fill — the #728 reset class the diff fixes for runs is left broken for cells
samples.evidence: The diff fixes run color/highlight resets by passing `undefined` (handled by `removedInlineStyleAttrs` + `tree.removeStyleByPath`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:144/1881). The cell path was not updated: `docs-table-context-menu.tsx:230` calls `editor.applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: "" })`; `serializeCellStyle` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:238) does `if (s.backgroundColor) attrs.backgroundColor = ...`, so the empty string is dropped from the attribute map, and `applyCellStyle` (line 2426) only calls `tree.styleByPath(...)` with no `removeStyleByPath`. Because `styleByPath` merges, the previous `backgroundColor` attribute survives in the CRDT: locally the cache shows `''` (renders as no fill), but the fill reappears for peers and after reload. Same root cause as issue #728, one call site away from the guard the diff added.

samples.summary: `resolveStoredColor` only collapses the bare `''` before the resolver, so the `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` form the docstring calls reachable lands on the docs default instead of the theme color
samples.evidence: `return resolve(c === '' ? undefined : c) || undefined;` — the pre-resolver normalization matches only the string `''`. For `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` (a shape the function's own doc comment and the new PPTX test both call reachable) slides' `makeColorResolver` → `resolveColor` (slides/src/model/theme.ts:100-116) returns `''`, which the trailing `|| undefined` turns into `undefined`, so `renderRun`/`renderListMarker` fall back to `theme.defaultColor` (docs near-black) rather than the deck theme's text color. That is exactly the dark-deck failure the comment says the 'before' half exists to prevent, just for the object arm.

samples.summary: List-marker color: `??` lets a cleared marker color (`''`) mask the inline color instead of being treated as unset
samples.evidence: `const colorSource = m?.color ?? firstInline?.color;` — `''` is not nullish, so a marker whose color was cleared to the legacy empty string shadows `firstInline.color` and the marker paints `theme.defaultColor` (the new test at test/view/render-list-marker.test.ts enshrines this) while the run text next to it paints e.g. `#FF9900`. Under the '' = unset rule this change establishes everywhere else, the marker should fall through to the inline's color.

samples.summary: `isTransparentAlpha` treats an empty/whitespace alpha as fully transparent, contradicting its own "unparseable ⇒ opaque" rule and dropping a visible color
samples.evidence: `Number('')` and `Number(' ')` are `0`, finite and `<= 0`, so `rgba(1,2,3,)` or `rgba(1,2,3, )` (group 4 matches `[^)]*`, which permits empty) is classified fully transparent and `toRgbHexColor` returns `undefined`, silently dropping the color from the DOCX/PPTX attribute. The doc comment states anything unparseable is treated as opaque "so a color the user can see is never dropped"; the empty alpha case violates that.
searchedFor: read isTransparentAlpha and the rgb regex in model/color.ts

samples.summary: `toRgbHexColor` recognises only comma-form numeric `rgb()/rgba()` and 3/6/8-digit hex, so several legal CSS forms that can reach the model are silently dropped from exports
samples.evidence: Unhandled: `#RGBA` 4-digit shorthand, percentage channels (`rgb(100%, 0%, 0%)`), the space-separated modern syntax (`rgb(255 0 0 / 50%)`), `hsl()`/`hwb()`/`oklch()`/`color()`. `view/clipboard.ts:150-155` copies `el.style.color`/`backgroundColor` verbatim from pasted HTML, and CSSOM preserves modern color functions rather than rewriting them to `rgb()`, so those runs now export with the color attribute omitted (visible color loss in DOCX/PPTX) where previously they were written verbatim. Converting or at least handling the space-separated/percentage forms would avoid the loss.

samples.summary: PPTX table cell fill and border colors bypass the new normalizer, so a non-hex imported color still reaches `<a:srgbClr val>`
samples.evidence: `colorFromStringOrTheme(border.color)` (line 118) and `colorFromStringOrTheme(cell.style.fill)` (line 128) wrap any string as `{ kind: 'srgb', value }`; `colorChildXml` (export/pptx/color.ts:35) only strips `#` and upper-cases, so a value that is not six hex digits (PPTX import of `<a:srgbClr val>` goes through `normalizeHex` but shape/border colors can also come from other paths) still lands in the attribute as an invalid `ST_HexColorRGB`. The diff routes only text runs through `toRgbHexColor`, leaving these sibling sinks on the old unvalidated path.

verdict.reason: Verified the whole chain independently. docs-table-context-menu.tsx:230 sends `{ backgroundColor: "" }`; editor.ts:3648-3671 and document.ts:856-863 forward it unmodified; yorkie-doc-store.ts:2406-2434 `applyCellStyle` calls only `tree.styleByPath(...)` with attrs from `serializeCellStyle` (line 233-246), whose `if (s.backgroundColor)` drops the empty string, so the merge-only styleByPath leaves the previous backgroundColor attribute on the CRDT node while the local cache is set to '' (line 2430). parseCellStyle (254-264) reads the stale value back for peers and after reload. No counterexample exists: the only removeStyleByPath calls are 1424/1881 (inline runs) and 2477 (applyCellSpan span keys); no cell-style removal helper exists anywhere (no removedCellStyleAttrs/clearCellStyle); buildCellNode (329-335) is reached only from updateTableCell (2387)/row builds (2347), not from applyCellStyle; markDirty is layout invalidation only. Existing tests (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2000-2029) cover set/merge but never a reset. Real correctness bug: user's reset silently fails to persist.

finding.summary: `resolveStoredColor` only collapses the bare `''` before the resolver, so the `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` form the docstring calls reachable lands on the docs default instead of the theme color
finding.evidence: `return resolve(c === '' ? undefined : c) || undefined;` — the pre-resolver normalization matches only the string `''`. For `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` (a shape the function's own doc comment and the new PPTX test both call reachable) slides' `makeColorResolver` → `resolveColor` (slides/src/model/theme.ts:100-116) returns `''`, which the trailing `|| undefined` turns into `undefined`, so `renderRun`/`renderListMarker` fall back to `theme.defaultColor` (docs near-black) rather than the deck theme's text color. That is exactly the dark-deck failure the comment says the 'before' half exists to prevent, just for the object arm.

verdict.reason: Verified as described. `resolveStoredColor` (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:49) normalizes the legacy empty color only via the strict string test `c === ''`, so the object form `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` reaches the resolver. In slides, `makeColorResolver` returns the deck `themeText` only for `c == null` (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:55) or the literal string `'#000000'` (line 57); an object goes to `resolveColor`, which for the srgb arm returns `color.value` verbatim — i.e. `''` (packages/slides/src/model/theme.ts:102-116). The trailing `|| undefined` then turns that into `undefined`, and `renderRun` / `renderListMarker` fall back to `theme.defaultColor` (packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:388-389, 555), which in slides is the docs `DefaultTheme` because `paintTextBody` calls `paintLayout` with no `theme` (text-renderer.ts:242; paint-layout.ts:108) and `DefaultTheme.defaultColor` is the near-black light ink (packages/docs/src/view/theme.ts:46-49). That is precisely the dark-deck failure the docstring at color.ts:33-38 says the "before" normalization exists to prevent, just for the object arm. Reachability of the shape is asserted by the repo itself (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:170-172 states the #728 reset reaches there "both as the bare string and as `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }`") and exercised by packages/slides/test/export/pptx/text.test.ts:110-117. No other guard collapses the empty srgb value before the resolver, so there is no already-guarded ground; the defect is a wrong-condition/inconsistent-normalization bug producing wrong rendered state, squarely in the correctness lane.

mergedFrom.summary: `hasColor` misses the object form of the cleared color, `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }`, which still serializes as `<a:srgbClr val=""/>`

finding.summary: PPTX export's new `hasColor` guard only filters the empty string; every other non-hex color string (CSS `rgb(...)` from HTML paste, color keywords) still reaches `<a:srgbClr val="…"/>` and produces a deck PowerPoint rejects
finding.evidence: `hasColor()` (text.ts:180) returns true for any non-empty string, so `storedColorToThemeColor` → `colorFromStringOrTheme` → `colorChildXml` (color.ts:35) emits `escapeXmlAttr(value.replace(/^#/,'').toUpperCase())`. For a run whose `style.color` is `rgb(255, 0, 0)` this writes `<a:srgbClr val="RGB(255, 0, 0)"/>` — not a valid `ST_HexColorRGB`, exactly the failure mode the DOCX half of this same commit fixed with `toDocxHexColor`. The value is reachable: slides text boxes run the docs `TextEditor` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:109), whose HTML-paste path assigns browser-normalized CSS verbatim — `style.color = el.style.color` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:151) and `style.backgroundColor = el.style.backgroundColor` (line 154). The delta hardened docs/DOCX against precisely this input but left the slides emitter guarding only `''`.

verdict.reason: The finding's central artifact does not exist: a repo-wide Grep for `hasColor` returns no matches, so there is no "guard that only filters the empty string" at packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:180. The actual code at text.ts:183-200 (`storedColorToThemeColor`) normalizes every string/srgb color through the shared `toRgbHexColor` (text.ts:188) and returns `undefined` when normalization fails, in which case callers (text.ts:281-298, 135-138) omit the color child entirely. `toRgbHexColor` (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:89-116) explicitly parses `rgb()`/`rgba()` (line 106-113) — `rgb(255, 0, 0)` becomes `FF0000` (test at packages/docs/test/model/color.test.ts:232) — and returns `undefined` for color keywords such as `red` (test line 248), `var(--fg)` (line 249) and `''` (line 246). Its return is `[0-9A-F]{6}` by construction, so `colorChildXml` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:35) can only ever receive a valid ST_HexColorRGB. The slides emitter therefore uses the same normalizer the reviewer claims only the DOCX side received (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:48). The described failure mode cannot occur.

finding.summary: `toDocxHexColor` silently discards alpha, so a fully transparent color (`rgba(r,g,b,0)` / `#RRGGBB00`) exports as an opaque solid shading instead of no shading
finding.evidence: Line 62 (`#RRGGBBAA` → `v.slice(0,6)`) and line 66-72 (`rgba(...)` → alpha group ignored via `(?:,[^)]*)?`) both drop the alpha channel unconditionally. `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` therefore yields `000000` and the exporter writes `<w:shd w:val="clear" w:color="auto" w:fill="000000"/>` — a solid black block behind text that is transparent on screen. This is reachable from the same HTML-paste source the doc comment cites (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:154 stores whatever CSS the browser hands back, including `rgba(...)` with alpha 0). Alpha 0 should map to "no fill" rather than to the RGB triple.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. `toDocxHexColor` in packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:47-49 contains no color parsing at all — it delegates to the shared `toRgbHexColor` (the finding's quoted lines 62 and 66-72 of that file are actually the `<w:rFonts>` ascii/eastAsia logic at docx-style-map.ts:58-74). In the real implementation (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:89-116) the fully-transparent case is explicitly special-cased, exactly as the finding asks: the `#RRGGBBAA` branch returns `undefined` when the alpha byte is `00` (color.ts:100) *before* reaching `v.slice(0,6)` (color.ts:101), so the slice is not unconditional; and the `rgba()` regex *captures* alpha as group 4 (`(?:,([^)]*))?`, color.ts:106 — not the non-capturing `(?:,[^)]*)?` quoted by the reviewer) and returns `undefined` via `isTransparentAlpha` for both number and percentage zero forms (color.ts:58-62, 108). The documented rule is stated at color.ts:80-84 and docx-style-map.ts:40-45. Both DOCX sinks are therefore safe: `<w:shd>` is only emitted behind `if (bgHex)` (docx-style-map.ts:99-102) and the table-cell fill also routes through `toDocxHexColor` (docx-exporter.ts:319), so no path writes `w:fill="000000"` for `rgba(0,0,0,0)`. Existing tests assert precisely the claimed-broken behavior is absent: `toDocxHexColor('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)')` and `toDocxHexColor('#11223300')` are `undefined` (docx-style-map.test.ts:116-117; color.test.ts:240-242). No duplicate/alternate implementation exists (grep for `toRgbHexColor`/`toDocxHexColor` shows a single definition at color.ts:89).
